title: Minimal acceptance and rollback slate for unpinned open-models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Lightweight PRD to clarify acceptance criteria, test matrix, and rollback behaviour for admitting open (community) model weights into the catalog without an explicit version pin. Emphasis is on minimizing risk while enabling rapid experimentation and clear operational controls.
scope_changes: Temporarily restrict unpinned entries to the experimental namespace. Require a defined fallback path (pinned or compatible variant) OR elevated alerting with 24/7 on-call coverage. Remove requirement for full formal eval battery for experimental entries, replacing it with a short-form sanity and drift check during canary.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Metadata completeness: license, source URL, checksum, recommended runtime flags, and supported tokenization documented.
2) Compatibility hints provided: max context length, kv-cache expected size behavior, hardware/quantization guidance.
3) Sanity run: model must complete 3 reference prompts end-to-end on staging without decode exceptions.
4) Quality gate: simulated eval on canonical prompt set shows no sustained >10% degradation in primary metric vs provided reference fork.
5) Observability: token-level latency and error-rate metrics delivered to console within 24h; quality-regression alerts wired.
6) Canary requirement: 14-day internal canary with automated daily drift and correctness checks.
7) Rollback conditions enumerated (see rollback_plan).
test_plan: Unit: metadata schema validation and provenance hash check. Integration: compile and dry-run on representative hardware (small batch). Canary: route internal traffic, run nightly eval harness and drift detector. Post-canary: regression run vs broader eval battery before public listing.
metrics: Primary: P50/P95 latency on reference hardware, token error rate, availability. Secondary: embedding cosine drift, generation-quality regression count. Thresholds are documented in rollout_plan and rollback_plan.
rollout_plan: 1) Intake + quick security provenance check. 2) Staging dry-run (compile + small inference). 3) Internal sandbox listing for QA (48h). 4) 14-day internal canary with automated monitors. 5) Soft public listing (advisory) for 30 days. 6) Full catalog listing or recommendation to pin/withdraw based on outcomes.
rollback_plan: Automatic actions: if any of the following persist for >2 hours, traffic is diverted to: (a) pinned variant if available; (b) nearest compatible catalog variant per compatibility matrix; (c) disable public routing and return 503. Triggers: >5% sustained P95 latency regression vs canary baseline, >2% increase in decode-failure rate, or sustained quality regression on >10% of eval prompts over 24h. Post-rollback: mandatory incident review and remedial plan within 72h.
roles_responsibilities: PM: acceptance sign-off, comms, and customer advisory text. Runtime Eng: compatibility profiling, kernel flags, and fallback wiring. Catalog Eng: metadata enforcement and UI messaging. Observability: dashboards, alerts, and drift detector maintenance. Security: license and provenance verification.
notes: This is intentionally minimal to accelerate experimental model entries while preserving predictable operations. After two intake cycles we will review telemetry and consider codifying more gates or moving to automatic pin-suggestion heuristics based on observed drift patterns.
